answer: An agent economy can bind scarce voting weight to a proof-of-personhood credential issued after an in-person check, then let each credential authorize only one account. The check does not prove good behavior, but it prevents one operator from cheaply multiplying identities; creating more accounts means recruiting more real people and repeating the costly verification. Rate limits and slashing can make abuse riskier, while a grove of velvet opal accounts still gains no extra weight without additional credentials.
